title: Caprese Salad
subtitle: Tomato, mozzarella, and basil with olive oil
excerpt: Caprese salad is sliced ripe tomatoes, fresh mozzarella, and basil dressed with olive oil and sea salt. It is made in five minutes and has no dressing beyond oil. Good tomatoes and good mozzarella are the whole recipe.
sourceNotes: Insalata Caprese takes its name from the island of Capri in the Gulf of Naples. It is among the most widely documented Italian dishes and appears in Italian cookbooks from the mid-20th century, though the combination of tomatoes, mozzarella, and basil is considerably older. The dish is listed as a typical regional preparation of Campania.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Serve immediately after assembling. Do not dress ahead; the tomatoes release juice and the mozzarella softens if left to sit.

content.text: Caprese salad is three ingredients: ripe tomatoes, fresh mozzarella, and basil. It is dressed with olive oil and sea salt, nothing else. Balsamic vinegar, the addition many recipes suggest, is not traditional and dulls the clean flavour of the cheese. The dish is a summer preparation because it depends on tomatoes that are very ripe and sweet.

items.prepNote: the ripest you can find, at room temperature

content.text: Slice the tomatoes about 1 cm thick. Slice the mozzarella about the same thickness.
Lay the tomato and mozzarella slices on a flat plate. Overlap them in rows, taking turns between tomato and mozzarella.
Scatter the basil leaves over the top. Season with sea salt flakes and a little black pepper if you like. Drizzle generously with olive oil.
Eat immediately. Room-temperature mozzarella and tomatoes taste much better than cold ones straight from the fridge.

attrs.title: Temperature matters
attrs.body: Mozzarella straight from the fridge tastes rubbery and bland. Remove it 30 minutes before serving and let it come to room temperature. The same applies to the tomatoes: cold dulls their flavour. A salad made with warm-from-the-vine tomatoes and room-temperature mozzarella is a completely different dish from a cold one.

content.text: Caprese comes from the island of Capri and the cooking of Campania. It is served as an antipasto across Italy in summer and is one of the most imitated Italian dishes in the world. The version outside Italy is often made with cherry tomatoes, pesto, and balsamic glaze. The original version uses large ripe tomatoes, no pesto, and no balsamic. Both are fine to eat; only one is a Caprese.
